macro_summary: Markets face a compressed 36-hour macro gauntlet: July PCE and Q2 GDP second estimate hit pre-market today, NVDA reports after the close tonight, and Fed Chair Warsh delivers his inaugural Jackson Hole keynote Friday August 28. September FOMC hike odds sit near 33-40% — a genuine coin-flip — with the market complacently pricing a neutral Warsh tone despite a split 9-3 FOMC dissent vote in July and core PCE running at 3.3% YoY, well above target. 10-year yields near multi-decade highs add a fragile backdrop for rate-sensitive growth equities heading into this event cluster.

ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ideas.thesis: NVDA appeared in all 6 overnight screens with unanimous high conviction — the strongest consensus signal of the session. The stock reports Q2 FY2027 earnings after the close tonight against a setup of 58/61 analysts rated Buy, a consensus PT of ~$305 vs. ~$212 last close (44% gap), upward EPS revisions of 6.7% over three months, and a 7-consecutive-session losing streak — the longest since 2022 — creating a potential mean-reversion beat catalyst. Forward P/E of ~21x is below the Nasdaq-100 average of ~25x despite guided 95-96% YoY revenue growth, with Vera Rubin GPU ramp and a $1T order book in focus. All runs favor defined-risk options (call spread or straddle) over outright stock given binary earnings risk and elevated implied volatility.
ideas.catalyst: Q2 FY2027 earnings report after market close today, August 26, 2026 — Vera Rubin ramp and $1T order book guidance the key incremental focus
ideas.edge: Consensus EPS of $2.09-$2.13 on $92B revenue (+96% YoY); 62-analyst avg PT of ~$305 vs ~$212 last close = 44% implied upside gap; forward P/E ~21x below Nasdaq-100 avg of ~25x; stock down 7 straight sessions — longest losing streak since 2022
ideas.bull_case: A beat-and-raise on Vera Rubin demand confirmation and $1T+ backlog commentary sparks a mean-reversion rally from a technically oversold 7-day drawdown, with the 44% analyst PT gap providing a long runway for re-rating.
ideas.bear_case: Post-earnings stock reactions have been muted or negative in the last four quarters despite beats ('sell the news'), and elevated IV means options decay rapidly — a guidance-in-line result may not be enough to reverse the losing streak.

ideas.name: SK Hynix Inc.
ideas.thesis: SKHY appeared in all 6 overnight screens with unanimous high conviction, making it the top non-NVDA consensus idea. As the dominant HBM memory supplier controlling ~57% of the HBM market, SKHY is the purest read-through play on tonight's NVDA print — a strong Vera Rubin demand confirmation from NVDA directly validates SK Hynix's order pipeline. The stock trades at ~$158.88 vs. a 13/13 analyst consensus PT of ~$247 (55% upside), has pulled back ~11% from its August 17 peak of ~$178 in a technically constructive higher-low structure, and carries a KRW 40 trillion share buyback (announced Aug 19) and Temasek sovereign wealth backing (confirmed Aug 12) as near-term support.
ideas.catalyst: NVDA Q2 FY2027 earnings tonight (Aug 26) as direct HBM demand read-through; Needham PT raise to $220 on Aug 25; KRW 40T buyback ongoing since Aug 19
ideas.edge: Consensus PT of ~$247-$252 vs. ~$159 ADR price = 55-75% analyst upside gap; 13/13 analysts rated Buy/Strong Buy; Q2 miss (-9.6% sell-off in late July) appears already digested; buyback provides downside support
ideas.bull_case: A strong NVDA beat with bullish Vera Rubin ramp commentary directly validates SK Hynix's HBM pipeline, triggering a re-rating toward consensus targets from a technically improved entry ~11% off the recent high, with the buyback cushioning any pullback.
ideas.bear_case: SKHY is a newly listed Nasdaq ADR with uncertain options liquidity for defined-risk plays; a disappointing NVDA print or cautious AI capex guidance would hit SKHY harder than more diversified semis, and the July Q2 miss shows execution risk remains.

ideas.name: Invesco QQQ Trust (Nasdaq-100 ETF)
ideas.thesis: QQQ appeared in 5 of 6 overnight screens as the preferred macro hedge vehicle for the full event cluster compressed into the next 36 hours: today's PCE/GDP print (8:30 AM ET), NVDA earnings tonight, and Fed Chair Warsh's inaugural Jackson Hole keynote Friday August 28. Markets have priced ~69% probability of a neutral Warsh tone, but September hike odds remain near 1-in-3 — meaning a hawkish surprise or hot PCE read could materially reprice the Nasdaq-100 lower. A straddle or strangle on QQQ captures directional ambiguity at defined cost and hedges both an NVDA sell-the-news reaction and a hawkish Fed surprise simultaneously.
ideas.catalyst: Fed Chair Warsh's inaugural Jackson Hole keynote, Friday August 28 ~10:00 AM ET; July PCE release pre-market today August 26 at 8:30 AM ET; NVDA earnings after close tonight
ideas.edge: September rate hike odds at ~33-40% (unresolved binary); 69% of fund managers priced neutral — asymmetric surprise value on any hawkish signal; QQQ already -0.76% Monday on chip weakness; straddle/strangle captures 1-3% directional move at defined premium cost
ideas.bull_case: A softer-than-expected PCE print combined with a strong NVDA beat and a measured Warsh tone relieves twin rate and earnings overhangs simultaneously, sending QQQ higher with the straddle's call leg capturing the upside.
ideas.bear_case: A neutral Warsh speech (the consensus case) with an in-line NVDA result leaves QQQ range-bound and the straddle loses on both legs via time decay — the biggest risk is a non-event outcome into expensive event vol.

ideas.name: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust
ideas.thesis: SPY appeared in 3 of 6 overnight screens as a complementary broad-market hedge to QQQ, focused specifically on the hawkish tail risk from Warsh's Friday speech. The July FOMC saw a 9-3 dissent vote, core PCE is running at 3.3% YoY — well above the 2% target — and September hike odds are near 40%, yet fund managers are overwhelmingly positioned for a neutral speech. A short-dated SPY put spread expiring post-August 28 offers cheap, defined-risk portfolio protection against the scenario where a new Fed chair surprises with a hawkish tone into the September 16-17 FOMC decision.
ideas.catalyst: Fed Chair Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote, Friday August 28 at 8:00-10:00 AM ET; September 16-17 FOMC decision 19 days later; July PCE data today August 26 at 8:30 AM ET
ideas.edge: 69% of fund managers pricing neutral Warsh tone — any hawkish deviation is an asymmetric surprise; 10-year yields near multi-decade highs; September hike odds near 40% (near coin-flip); S&P 500 already showing 3 consecutive down weeks recently
ideas.bull_case: Warsh delivers a measured, neutral speech and PCE comes in soft, relieving both the rate and inflation overhang and allowing SPY to rally through the event window with the put spread expiring near worthless at defined cost.
ideas.bear_case: A hawkish Warsh signal — such as openness to a September hike — combined with a hot PCE print creates a rate shock that drops SPY materially, validating the put spread hedge and delivering asymmetric protection for long-tech portfolios.

ideas.name: Apple Inc.
ideas.thesis: AAPL appeared in 2 of 6 overnight screens — at the minimum threshold — as a lower-beta way to participate in any AI hardware halo from tonight's NVDA print. Apple launched an AI-developer-targeted Mac Mini and Mac Studio refresh on August 25, signaling a deliberate enterprise AI pivot just ahead of the NVDA print. At ~$310 with contained volatility relative to pure semis, AAPL suits moderate-risk swing profiles seeking sector exposure without the full binary earnings risk of NVDA itself.
ideas.catalyst: AI-developer-focused Mac Mini and Mac Studio launched August 25, 2026; NVDA earnings tonight as sector read-through for enterprise AI hardware demand; softer PCE print today would add a rates tailwind
ideas.edge: Stock at ~$310 with lower vol than pure semis; AI developer hardware cycle just initiated; indirect beneficiary of NVDA beat scenario with lower binary risk; benefits from a rates-friendly PCE outcome given lower duration sensitivity vs. high-multiple semis
ideas.bull_case: A strong NVDA print validating AI capex demand, combined with a soft PCE read, lifts AAPL on both the AI hardware halo effect and a rate relief narrative, with the new Mac product cycle providing an idiosyncratic catalyst to outperform broad tech.
ideas.bear_case: AAPL's AI hardware exposure is indirect and the Mac refresh may be incremental rather than transformative — if NVDA disappoints or Warsh turns hawkish Friday, AAPL is not immune and the low-conviction appearance in only 2 of 6 screens reflects genuine uncertainty about the near-term edge.
